note: Every file in conformance/toml_rejected/ makes gnomon's TOML parser throw, and this index pins WHERE. 'line' is the 1-based line the error names and 'offending' is the text it quotes; the full message is `line <line>: cannot parse <JSON-quoted offending>. Expected a [table] header, a [[array]] header, or key = value.`, and loadConfig prefixes it with `.gnomon/<filename> `. Asserted by packages/gnomon-core/src/config.test.ts, which also fails if a fixture exists with no case here.
why_the_line_number_matters: The throw exists because these lines used to be silently skipped: `[roles.verifier` with the bracket missing dropped the header and hoisted its keys to the top level, so the role vanished while its bash_allow became a root key read by nothing. Naming the file and line is the whole remedy, so a wrong line number is a real regression -- hence pinning it. Note cases 04, 05 and 11, where the named line is one or two PAST the construct that caused the failure, because the parser is line-based and reports where it stopped.

cases.construct: a [table] header missing its closing bracket
a dotted key in key position (a.b = ...)
an inline # comment on a [table] or [[array]] header
cases.offending: [tools] # the tools this role may call

cases.construct: a dash in a key (accepted in a table NAME, rejected in a key)
a line that is neither a header nor key = value
cases.offending: the verifier should be strict about tests

cases.construct: a ] inside a string inside a MULTI-LINE array (fine on one line)
